current_activity: designated XIX Corps reserve on Hill 219 west of Vire
notes: Event date: 6 August 1944 (Breakout-23 p451). Event definition: Corlett decided it was unprofitable to keep using the 2d Armored Division combat commands to spearhead the infantry attacks; he instructed Brooks to move the division off the roads so the 28th and 29th Divisions could pass through; the armored division, except CCA on Hill 219, now designated XIX Corps reserve, assembled and prepared to move into the VII Corps zone. Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). In the days before this, on 2 August, after Tessy was secured, Breakout-15 p304 says CCA reverted to 2d Armored Division control; the same day, Breakout-23 p449, the 29th Division with CCA attached attacked from the Percy-Tessy line toward Vire (treated as a same-day mission change, not a sourced gap in the 29th attachment). The battle for Vire started on 5 August; the 2d Armored Division CCA spearhead was struck at Martilly, and other tanks of CCA secured Hill 219, west of Vire (Breakout-23 p450-451). Breakout-24 p471: the 2d Armored Division (less CCA, which remained near Vire) departed the XIX Corps sector shortly after midnight, 6 August. Relationship: the attachment to the 29th Division (CR1313) ends on this date; CCA remains under XIX Corps (CR0177) as corps reserve; organic to the 2nd Armored Division. The day CCA later rejoined the division is not stated. Location: Hill 219, west of Vire / Vire Normandie, Calvados (place PL1272) with a precision of 5 km (the hill is named but not given its own coordinates; the point is the town centroid).
